paper.title: Damned if You Do(n't): How Epistemic Technology Spoils Expertise
paper.authors: Ayman Ajaj, Mayur Joshi, Mathieu Bouchard

tiles.label: Your case
tiles.sub: Radiologist at a community hospital; adoption, others · second judge: Slopped (disagree) · 5/5 quotes verified verbatim

tiles.label: Damned if you don't
tiles.sub: the quadrant the same audience points to had you made the opposite adoption choice

tiles.label: Two-judge agreement (κ)
tiles.sub: 95% CI [0.82, 1.00] on 36 comments · stance κ 0.89, locus κ 0.96

figures.title: Where does your situation sit in the 2×2?
figures.caption: ★ = the overall reading of your case. Dots = each of your statements coded separately by the two judges. The dashed arrow points to the mirror quadrant: the 'damned if you don't' alternative.

figures.title: Can the 2×2 be coded reliably?
figures.caption: Two LLM judges (different models, same codebook: the paper's definitions) coded every comment independently. Counts reflect the corpus as written, not how common each form is in the world.

figures.title: Where do the judges disagree?
figures.caption: Rows = judge A, columns = judge B. Off-diagonal cells are the ambiguous cases worth reading.
